Set up a self-hosted runner, step by step

## Usage

`circleci runner init [<namespace>/<name>] [flags]`

## Arguments

`<namespace>/<name>` is the resource class to create, in an existing namespace; prompted for if omitted.

## Flags

| Flag                   | Description                                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--description string` | description of the resource class                                                              |
| `-f, --force`          | accept the runner terms without a confirmation prompt                                          |
| `--jq string`          | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`)              |
| `--json`               | Output as JSON                                                                                 |
| `--org string`         | Organization slug (e.g. gh/myorg) or UUID; defaults to git remote                              |
| `--platform string`    | where the agent will run: debian\|rpm\|macos\|windows\|docker\|kubernetes (prompts when unset) |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- Walk through setup, answering prompts: 
  `circleci runner init`
- Set up a Linux runner for an org: 
  `circleci runner init my-org/linux-runner --platform debian --org gh/my-org`
- Capture the token and steps for automation: 
  `circleci runner init my-org/ci --platform docker --force --json`

## Details

Accept the runner terms if needed, create a resource class and token, then print
install steps for your platform. Nothing is installed for you.
JSON fields: org_id, terms_already_accepted, resource_class_id, resource_class,
token_id, token, platform, steps, job_config, docs_url
